_strings.@@9964157f0bc9: Two Wage Earner Credit — Married couples filing jointly when both spouses have earned income taxed to South Carolina. Not allowed for filing statuses Single, Married Filing Separately, or Head of Household. If either spouse's qualified earned income is zero or less, the credit cannot be taken.
_strings.@@d2ebbec48149: Tuition Tax Credit — A SC resident student (or a parent/legal guardian/other person who can claim the student as a dependent and who paid the tuition) attending a qualifying SC 2-year or 4-year college/university, meeting the I-319 requirements (SC high school diploma or qualifying equivalent, enrollment within 12 months, in-state tuition rate, credit-hour minimums, no disqualifying scholarships/convictions/defaults; claimable at most four consecutive years).
_strings.@@d8ee2b9ea0e0: Child and Dependent Care Credit — Full-year SC residents who incurred federal child and dependent care expenses (reported on federal Form 2441). Part-year residents/nonresidents qualify only if they are residents of a state that offers a comparable credit to nonresidents, and then only on a prorated basis. Cannot be claimed if filing status is Married Filing Separately.
_strings.@@e18bb75e0445: Treaty conformity — SC conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from SC income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the SC return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: SC1040 line 1 starts from FEDERAL TAXABLE INCOME ("Enter federal taxable income from your federal form. If zero or less, enter zero" - 2024 SC1040, line 1). Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal taxable income before the SC return begins. SC's additions to income (SC1040 lines a-e) do NOT include any add-back of tax-treaty-exempt income. The only foreign-related add-back is on line e ("Add back foreign area allowances, cost of living allowances, and income from US possessions" - 2024 SC1040 instructions), which is distinct from income exempt under a federal income tax treaty and does not re-capture treaty income. Because treaty-exempt income is neither in the federal taxable-income starting point nor added back, it is NOT re-taxed by SC -> conforms. (SC conforms to the IRC as amended through December 31, 2023, except as otherwise provided.)

The TC-60 instructs the taxpayer to STOP (no credit) if they were not a full-year SC resident or were not eligible for the federal EITC.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: 2024 Form SC1040, line 6: 'TAX on your South Carolina Income Subject to Tax (see SC1040TT)'. Line 5 (South Carolina Income Subject to Tax) = line 1 federal taxable income ('Enter federal taxable income from your federal form') + line 2 SC additions (lines a-e) - line 4 SC subtractions (lines f-w, including the line w dependent exemption this block ships). This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: TY2024 RATE STEP-DOWN: the top rate fell from 6.4% to 6.2% (the annual Act 228 of 2022 reduction toward 6%; SCDOR: '0 to a top rate of 6.2% for tax year 2024'), the bracket bounds indexed to $3,460/$17,330 (from $3,330/$16,680), and the subtraction constants became $104/$659 (from $100/$670). Base guidance: supply SC1040 line 5 (South Carolina Income Subject to Tax) BEFORE the line w dependent exemption — i.e. line 1 federal TAXABLE income (federal 1040 line 15; the federal standard/itemized deduction is already embedded, never subtract it again) plus SC additions (lines a-e) minus the other SC subtractions (lines f-v) — and pass dependents_count so the op subtracts the shipped $4,790-per-dependent line w amount to reproduce line 5. South Carolina has NO personal exemption and NO state standard deduction of its own. Adjudication note (two-pass): pass 1 = the 2024 SC1040TT (mandatory tables below $100,000 + the printed $100,000-or-more schedule '6.2% minus $659'); pass 2 = the 2024 SC4972's printed '2024 Tax Computation Schedule' ($0-$3,460 0%; $3,460-$17,330 3% times the amount minus $104; $17,330+ 6.2% times the amount minus $659). Both passes agree on every bound and rate. NOTE: the SC1040 instruction booklet itself prints NO bracket dollar bounds — the SC4972 schedule is the official in-form statement of them. CRITICAL — SC's filed arithmetic is a SUBTRACTION METHOD, not marginal accumulation: the official computation is 'rate x ENTIRE income - constant', and the printed constants are ROUNDED in the taxpayer's favor ($104 vs the exact marginal $103.80; $659 vs the exact $658.36). Pure marginal accumulation (this engine) therefore comes out up to ~$1 HIGHER than the filed method above $17,330 — e.g. $101,000 -> engine $5,604 vs the SC1040TT's own printed example $5,603 (6.2% x $101,000 - $659). The filed return must use the SC1040TT table or the $100,000+ schedule; treat this block's output as an estimate within ~$1-3 (table bands add their own few-dollar spread). Tax-table mandate: taxable income under $100,000 MUST use the SC1040TT tax tables (2024 SC1040 instructions, Line 6); the tables are built in $50/$100 bands from the subtraction formulas at band midpoints (rounded), so a row can differ from exact arithmetic by a few dollars in either direction (e.g. exact $12,000 -> engine $256, but the $12,000-$12,100 row prints $258). Taxable income of $100,000 or more MUST use the rate schedule (6.2% x line 5 - $659). ONE rate schedule for every filing status — the SC1040TT states 'Use this Tax Rate Schedule for any filing status claimed on the SC1040'; the identical schedule is duplicated across all four statuses here, copied, not derived (qualifying surviving spouse included). Zero-rate floor: the first $3,460 of SC taxable income is taxed at 0% (the schema's zero-rate bottom bracket, like OH/MS) — a filer at or below $3,460 owes $0 with no exemption needed. Credits are NOT modeled (tax credits, not base reductions): Two Wage Earner Credit (line 12, .007 x up to $50,000 of the lower-earning spouse's qualified earned income, max $350), Child and Dependent Care Credit (line 11, 7% of the federal expense, max $210/$420), SC Earned Income Tax Credit (125% of the federal EITC via TC-60 -> SC1040TC -> line 13, nonrefundable), and the refundable Tuition Tax Credit (line 21, Form I-319). Out of scope on the same return: TAX on Lump-Sum Distribution (line 7, SC4972) is a separate additional tax; Active Trade or Business income electing the flat 3% rate (Form I-335) is excluded from this schedule; both are computed on their own forms.
